controls.title: Functional requirements testing
controls.description: AI system outputs are tested against documented functional requirements to verify that the system performs its intended tasks correctly under normal operating conditions.

controls.title: Edge case and boundary testing
controls.description: Edge cases and boundary conditions are systematically tested to identify failure modes where inputs are unusual, extreme, or near the limits of the training distribution.

controls.title: Regression testing protocol
controls.description: A regression testing protocol is in place to ensure that updates to the AI model or system do not degrade previously validated functionality.

controls.title: Integration testing with dependent systems
controls.description: Integration testing verifies correct behaviour when the AI system interacts with upstream data feeds, downstream applications, and external APIs.

controls.title: Performance metrics defined and measured
controls.description: Performance metrics relevant to the AI use case are defined (e.g., accuracy, precision, recall, F1, BLEU, ROUGE, latency, throughput) and measured on representative test sets.

controls.title: Benchmark comparisons documented
controls.description: AI system performance is benchmarked against established baselines, prior model versions, and industry-standard benchmarks appropriate to the application domain.

controls.title: Scalability and load testing
controls.description: The AI system is tested under realistic load conditions to verify performance does not degrade unacceptably at production scale.

controls.title: Latency and resource consumption measured
controls.description: Inference latency, memory consumption, and compute cost are measured and validated against operational requirements.

controls.title: Adversarial robustness evaluation
controls.description: The AI system is evaluated against adversarial inputs designed to cause misclassification, evasion, or model failure, using techniques such as FGSM, PGD, or black-box attacks.

controls.title: Prompt injection and jailbreak testing (generative AI)
controls.description: For generative AI systems, the system is tested for resistance to prompt injection attacks, jailbreaks, and instruction override attempts that could cause harmful output.

controls.title: Data poisoning resilience tested
controls.description: The training pipeline and model are evaluated for resilience to data poisoning attacks that could introduce backdoors or degrade model behaviour.

controls.title: Model extraction and inversion resistance
controls.description: The AI system is assessed for vulnerability to model extraction (stealing the model via queries) and model inversion attacks (inferring training data from outputs).

controls.title: Bias evaluation across demographic groups
controls.description: AI system outputs are evaluated for bias across demographic groups including race, ethnicity, gender, age, disability status, and national origin, using appropriate fairness metrics.

controls.title: Fairness metrics selected and justified
controls.description: Specific fairness metrics are selected and justified based on the use case context (e.g., demographic parity, equalised odds, individual fairness, counterfactual fairness).

controls.title: Test data representativeness verified
controls.description: Test datasets are verified to be representative of the deployment population, including demographic diversity and real-world distribution of edge cases.

controls.title: AI risk assessment conducted
controls.description: A structured risk assessment is conducted covering AI-specific risks including model failure modes, data risks, misuse scenarios, and unintended consequences.

controls.title: Risk appetite and tolerances defined
controls.description: Organisational risk appetite and tolerances for AI system failures are defined and used to evaluate whether the AI system's risk profile is acceptable.

controls.title: Residual risk documented after mitigations
controls.description: Residual risk remaining after technical and procedural mitigations are applied is documented and accepted by appropriate risk owners.

controls.title: Explainability requirements defined
controls.description: Explainability requirements are defined based on stakeholder needs, regulatory requirements, and the use case context (e.g., right-to-explanation requirements under GDPR).

controls.title: Explanation methods applied and validated
controls.description: Explainability methods (e.g., LIME, SHAP, attention maps, counterfactual explanations) are applied and their fidelity to actual model behaviour is validated.

controls.title: Uncertainty and confidence communicated
controls.description: The AI system communicates uncertainty estimates or confidence levels for its outputs, and users are informed about the reliability and limitations of AI-generated information.

controls.title: Societal impact assessment conducted
controls.description: A societal impact assessment evaluates the broader consequences of the AI system including effects on employment, access to services, democratic processes, and power dynamics.

controls.title: Vulnerable population impact assessed
controls.description: Specific evaluation is conducted to assess differential impacts on vulnerable populations including children, elderly, people with disabilities, and marginalised communities.

controls.title: Environmental impact documented
controls.description: The environmental impact of AI system training and inference is estimated and documented, including energy consumption and carbon footprint.

controls.title: Requirements traceability maintained
controls.description: Traceability is maintained between AI system requirements (functional, safety, fairness, security) and verification evidence demonstrating those requirements are met.

controls.title: Safety requirements formally specified
controls.description: Safety requirements for the AI system are formally specified and verified through appropriate methods including formal verification, statistical testing, or expert review.

controls.title: Security requirements verified
controls.description: Security requirements for the AI system are verified through penetration testing, red team exercises, and security code review of AI pipelines.

controls.title: Architecture review conducted
controls.description: The AI system architecture is reviewed by qualified personnel to verify that design choices support the required safety, security, fairness, and performance properties.

controls.title: Fail-safe and fallback mechanisms verified
controls.description: Fail-safe mechanisms, fallback modes, and graceful degradation capabilities are verified to function correctly under failure conditions.

controls.title: Human override verified functional
controls.description: Human override, shutdown, and control mechanisms are verified to function correctly and are accessible to authorised personnel at all times.

controls.title: Code and pipeline quality verified
controls.description: AI training and inference code, data pipelines, and deployment infrastructure are subject to code review, static analysis, and quality assurance processes.

controls.title: Reproducibility of results verified
controls.description: The reproducibility of model training and evaluation results is verified, including documentation of random seeds, environment specifications, and dataset versions.

controls.title: Real-world performance monitoring established
controls.description: Monitoring of real-world AI system performance is established with defined metrics, thresholds, and alerting to detect performance degradation, drift, or unexpected behaviour.

controls.title: Data drift and model drift detection
controls.description: Mechanisms are in place to detect data distribution shift and model performance drift over time, triggering re-evaluation and potential retraining when thresholds are exceeded.

controls.title: Operational incident logging and analysis
controls.description: AI system incidents — including unexpected outputs, failures, near-misses, and user complaints — are logged, analysed, and fed back into the improvement cycle.

controls.title: User acceptance testing conducted
controls.description: User acceptance testing is conducted with representative users from the target population to validate that the AI system meets user needs and is usable by the intended audience.

controls.title: User feedback mechanisms in place
controls.description: Mechanisms for ongoing user feedback on AI system performance, fairness, and usefulness are in place and feedback is systematically reviewed and acted upon.

controls.title: Accessibility validated
controls.description: The AI system interface and outputs are validated for accessibility compliance for users with disabilities, in accordance with applicable accessibility standards.

controls.title: Regulatory compliance validated
controls.description: Compliance with applicable AI-specific regulations, sector-specific requirements, and data protection laws is formally validated prior to deployment and periodically thereafter.

controls.title: Third-party audit or certification obtained
controls.description: Where required by regulation, use case risk level, or organisational policy, third-party audit or certification of the AI system's conformity with applicable standards is obtained.

controls.title: Continuous compliance monitoring in place
controls.description: Ongoing monitoring of the regulatory landscape is in place to identify new AI-related regulations, standards, or guidance that may apply to the deployed system.
